$comment: The point-change benchmark's tasks. Each is a change a user asks of a deck they already have: `request` is their words (what a real agent is given, with the deck), `moves` what the scripted author writes into the pages file, one move a compile - a move after the first is made only when the compile before it refused - and `accept` what the revised deck is held to. An edit is `{ page, replace }` or `{ page, title }` on a carried page (`reset: true` writes the page's `replace` afresh, where a move corrects the one before), `{ page, set }` to give a page a type, `{ deck }` to set deck-level keys, or `{ sources }` to add to the citation registry beside them. `accept.edits` are the changes the request asks for, as `{ old, new }`: a line that differs on an edited slide and is not the source line with them made is an edit nobody asked for. `accept.prints` reads a slide's words, or its speaker notes with `notes: true`; `accept.retitled` lists the slides whose title must no longer be the source's, whatever words the author chose - a slide number, or `{ slide, says }` where the new title must use those words; `accept.refusedFor` the codes the first compile must refuse the first move for. `critic` has the scripted critic find something (`aboutImported`: a finding about a slide the revision did not change), and `deliver: true` carries the run past the review packet to an accepted delivery with a scripted reviewer.

tasks.request: FY26 revenue has been restated from £12.4m to £12.6m. Update the deck wherever it states the figure and change nothing else.

moves.note: The summary states the figure, so the author changes it there.
The compile names the closing slide, which still prints the old figure, and the table's total, which states the same quantity under "Revenue (£m)".

tasks.request: Slide 4's title is a label. Retitle it to say what the table shows: London grows fastest on the thinnest margin.

moves.note: A title is the slide's own text: it is rewritten in place.

tasks.request: Redraw the pie on slide 7 as a donut, with a title that says what it shows. Leave the other slides as they are.

moves.note: A chart is redrawn by giving its page a type: the runtime composes that one page, from the values the inventory holds.

set.title: Wholesale is now 22% of sales, more than twice delivery
set.why: Four channels of one year's sales are parts of a whole; the donut keeps the slide's reading and sets the shares side by side.

settles.what: Share of FY26 sales by channel

set.adds: The points say which channels carry the stores and why wholesale matters to the plan.
points: Wholesale is 22% of sales, up from 16% in FY22, and it is the one channel that grows without a new lease
In store and takeaway together are 68% of sales, so the estate still carries the business
Delivery is the smallest channel at 10% and the only one that pays a commission to a platform
